object.name: Modeling Worker v0.12｜E3 Automotive Application Benchmark

decision_question: Can the merged v0.12 relationship-driven surface compiler consume an automotive application with independently controllable hood, cabin, shoulder, rear-haunch, lower-body and termination volumes while preserving surface fairness and improving application-level proportion/form?
locked_variables: wheelbase / track package inherited from accepted v0.11 benchmark
broad overall length / width / height class
deterministic receipts and Machine / Visual / Project QA separation
E2 precision-aware multi-patch C2 method evidence
open_variables: independent low-frequency Surface Source architecture for hood / cowl versus cabin crown
independent cabin gesture rather than lifting one center dome
independent shoulder acceleration and rear-haunch buildup
lower-body / rocker counter-tension to shoulder mass
front and rear termination volume styling while preserving existing C2/fairness boundaries
fixed-view visual legibility of each semantic edit
next_allowed_action: Rebuild the E3 application Surface Source architecture so hood/cowl, cabin, shoulder/rear-haunch, lower-body and terminations have genuinely independent low-frequency source controls. Re-run the same Decision Question at working fidelity; do not open PAP or Promotion and do not add secondary detail/CMF to mask the architecture failure.
